items.title: BHP signs $4.3B silver streaming deal with Wheaton Precious Metals

featured_image.name: BHP Group signs silver streaming agreement with Wheaton Precious Metals

items.description:
BHP Group has entered into a $4.3 billion silver streaming agreement with Wheaton Precious Metals, marking what the mining giant describes as the largest streaming deal to date by upfront value.[1][2]

Under the agreement announced Tuesday alongside BHP's half-year results, the Australian miner will deliver silver from its 33.75% stake in Peru's Antamina mine to Wheaton in exchange for an upfront payment of $4.3 billion at completion. Upon closing, expected on or about April 1, 2026, Wheaton will receive a combined 67.5% of all silver produced from Antamina, doubling its current exposure from the 33.75% it already receives under an existing stream with Glencore.[3][2][4][5]

items.title: Google DeepMind says AlphaFold now used by 3 million researchers

featured_image.name: Google DeepMind to open UK research lab for discovery of new ...

items.description:
Google DeepMind leaders revealed this weekend that the company's AI-powered protein structure database has reached more than 3 million researchers across 190 countries, a milestone that underscores how artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific discovery worldwide.

In a commentary published in Fortune ahead of the India AI Impact Summit, DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis and Google Senior Vice President James Manyika outlined how the freely available AlphaFold Protein Database has become a standard tool for scientists tackling pressing global challenges. More than one-third of those researchers are based in low- and middle-income countries, according to the executives.[1][2]

items.title: Canada moves to bridge EU and Pacific trade blocs

featured_image.name: Canada's Carney aims to lead new global trading order less ...

items.description:
Prime Minister Mark Carney is pursuing negotiations to forge links between the European Union and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), a move that could unite nearly 40 nations in a coordinated framework to counter American protectionism.

Politico reported Monday that the Canadian government is spearheading talks between the 27-member EU and the 11-nation CPTPP to explore harmonized "rules of origin" that would allow manufacturers across both blocs to trade goods and components more smoothly through a mechanism called cumulation. If formalized, this arrangement would create an integrated trade architecture spanning both sides of the globe, designed to reduce vulnerability to tariff threats from Washington.[1][2]

items.title: Italy's Meloni publicly rejects German chancellor's MAGA criticism

featured_image.name: Far-right leader Giorgia Meloni named as Italy's first ...

items.description:
The alliance between Italy and Germany that emerged as a new force in European politics faces its first test after Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni publicly disagreed with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over his criticism of the American MAGA movement, exposing divergent visions of transatlantic relations just weeks after the leaders pledged closer cooperation.

"I do not agree" with Merz's remarks against MAGA culture, Meloni told Corriere della Sera and other Italian newspapers on February 15, returning from the African Union Assembly in Addis Ababa. While she endorsed Merz's call for Europe to strengthen its security capabilities and build a "European pillar of NATO," Meloni declined to echo his broader critique of the American political movement.[1][2]

items.title: Finland warns Russia is building military bases on its border

featured_image.name: Russia reinforcing nuclear and Arctic assets near Finnish ...

items.description:
Finnish Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen warned this weekend that Russia is reinforcing its strategic nuclear presence in the Arctic and constructing new military facilities along Finland's border, signaling an intensifying security threat to Europe's northern flank.

"Russia has most of their biggest strategic capabilities in nuclear, submarines, long-range bombers in the Kola Peninsula area," Häkkänen told Euronews on the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference, which concluded Sunday. "They are building new military facilities along our border, the same as during the Cold War. It would be wise to watch the Arctic and build Arctic capabilities."[1]

The Kola Peninsula, a 100,000-square-kilometer region in far northwestern Russia, hosts the majority of the country's sea-based strategic nuclear arsenal, including submarines and long-range aviation assets.[2][3]

items.title: Cuba activates 1990s-era rationing plan as Trump oil blockade deepens

featured_image.name: Cuba to increase rationing amid shortages

items.description:
Cuba is facing its most severe fuel shortage since the collapse of the Soviet Union as the Trump administration's oil blockade deepens, prompting the communist government to activate emergency rationing measures while Washington simultaneously delivers humanitarian aid through the Catholic Church.

The Cuban government has announced it is implementing what it calls "Option Zero," a contingency plan conceived during the 1990s Special Period that contemplates extreme rationing, local food self-sufficiency, and the use of animal traction for transport. President Miguel Díaz-Canel recently confirmed the country has entered this phase, pledging to guarantee seven pounds of rice monthly per person while prioritizing locally produced goods.[1]

items.title: Top fund manager warns most software firms won't survive AI

featured_image.name: Fund Beating 99% of Peers Sees Few Software Firms Surviving ...

items.description:
A fund manager whose portfolio has outperformed 99% of competitors is sounding the alarm on software stocks, warning that artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to the industry and that only a handful of companies will survive the coming disruption.

"We think application software faces an existential threat from AI," said Nick Evans, whose $12 billion global technology fund at Polar Capital beat 99% of peers over the past year and 97% over five years, in comments reported by Bloomberg on Sunday.[1]

The warning comes as software stocks have suffered a brutal start to 2026. An exchange-traded fund tracking the U.S. software sector has plummeted more than 21% this year, according to data from S3 Partners, while hedge funds have generated $24 billion in profits by betting against the sector. The software industry has seen roughly $1 trillion wiped from its market capitalization since late January, sparked by fears that AI large language models could disintermediate traditional enterprise applications.[2][3][4]

items.title: EU's Kallas rejects US criticism, urges Europe to 'reclaim agency'

featured_image.name: Kaja Kallas attends Munich Security Conference | News | ERR

items.description:
The 62nd Munich Security Conference concluded Sunday with European leaders sending a clear message: the continent must take greater responsibility for its own defense amid shifting transatlantic dynamics. Over three days of discussions, top officials outlined plans for increased military spending, nuclear deterrence cooperation, and reduced dependence on Washington.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas rejected American criticism of Europe, pushing back against suggestions that "woke and decadent Europe" faces "civilizational erasure." Speaking at the conference's closing session, Kallas outlined three priorities: defending Europe starting with Ukraine, securing the neighborhood through EU enlargement, and building global partnerships. She warned that Russia "must not gain more at the negotiating table than it has achieved on the battlefield."[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Russia offers to halt strikes if Ukraine holds elections

featured_image.name: Russia revives election-day truce offer, proposes UN rule for Ukraine

items.description:
Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin announced Saturday that Moscow is prepared to suspend airstrikes on election day if Ukraine holds presidential polls, reiterating an earlier offer from President Vladimir Putin while questioning the legitimacy of President Volodymyr Zelensky's government.

The announcement comes days before a new round of trilateral talks between Russia, the United States, and Ukraine scheduled for February 17-18 in Geneva, and as Washington continues pressing Kyiv to hold elections as a condition for U.S. security guarantees.
